summary.intent: Standardize sidebar navigation icons in the web app — replacing a mix of emoji/Unicode strings and SVG elements with a single consistent approach (all inline SVGs with currentColor).
summary.outcome: All 4 sidebar icons (folder, shared/link, bin/trash, settings/gear) were converted to stroke-based inline SVGs. A PR was opened (FSM1/cipher-box#436), merged to main, and a follow-up CI fix was made to the 'Verify API Spec' workflow to handle version string diffs in generated TS files on the release-please branch.

repo: Sidebar icons were stored as Unicode emoji strings in an ICON_MAP in NavItem.tsx, not as icon library components or SVGs — an unusual pattern that caused visual inconsistency.

The 'Verify API Spec' CI job does an exact diff of regenerated TS client files, which causes false failures on the release-please branch when the version bumps because generated file headers include the spec version string.
release-please is configured (release-please-config.json) and bumps versions; this interacts with the API spec verification workflow in a way that requires ignoring version comment lines in the diff.
The project uses commitlint with conventional commits (type(scope): description) — both the fix commit and docs commit passed validation.

code.finding: ICON_MAP was changed from Unicode emoji strings to inline SVG ReactNode elements using currentColor and strokeWidth='1.2' for consistency.
.nav-item-icon was changed from font-based text styling to a flex container (16x16px) to properly host SVG elements.
Verify API Spec job needed a fix to ignore the OpenAPI spec version comment line in generated TS files to prevent false failures on release-please version bump branches.

workflow: The GSD executor spawned two separate worktrees and made commits in each; manual cherry-pick onto a feature branch was required to consolidate the changes before pushing the PR.
When executors use worktrees, artifacts (SUMMARY.md etc.) must be manually copied back to the main repo before committing planning docs.

The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code runtime bug can cause executor agents to report failure even when commits and summary files were successfully created — always verify by checking git log and file existence.

friction: Executor split work across two separate worktrees, requiring manual cherry-pick and artifact copying to produce a clean feature branch — the workflow didn't handle multi-worktree consolidation automatically.
The 'Verify API Spec' CI failure on the release-please branch was a pre-existing issue that surfaced after the merge, requiring a separate unplanned fix commit.
open_items: CI fix for Verify API Spec (version string in generated TS diff) was committed but the transcript ends before confirming it passes on the release-please branch — should verify the next CI run succeeds.
The release-please-config.json was modified (69 insertions) in the same main merge — the scope and intent of those changes are not captured in this session.
